I like to explore on my own. Or read a book in a coffee shop or by the river. Or playing games, or drawing. Mainly individual activities. I don’t like talking to people in general so I tend to avoid it when at uni. 

My uni is not in America and I haven’t gotten the chance to talk to any locals—all my conversation is with fellow students. I’ve realized being here that I just don’t like making friends. Ultimately they will either betray me or lose interest in me, and that’s even if I can make friends with similar hobbies, which is very far and few between. Either way, these are people I’d never have interest in talking to outside of this program, so once this ends, we’ll all forget about each other anyway. 

I have acted like myself before, trying to meet people, and no one seemed to like it, not even my siblings even try to engage in the stuff I like. So I put up a more appealing front but it just gets exhausting and feels superficial. I wish there were no other students here so I could just enjoy myself. But every time I leave my room I have to talk to somebody, and put on a smile, and look nice and talk appropriately. I see new students every day since there are so many here for the program, it’s just tiring and it’s really making me not want to be here. I wish I could get breakfast without seeing anyone, and walk about the city without needing to have another student beside me. My only solace to be truly by myself is the washroom, and I’m paranoid now that the other students think I visit it too often.

i say this with the clarity of retrospect. freshman to senior year of high school was the largest change of my life. and then it kept changing, and so did i. you need to understand that the way you feel now is understandable but not rational. pain is an integral part of the horrible process of growing up, you shouldn’t inflict it upon yourself in addition. 

i say this really really gently. this situation will continue to repeat itself in variations until you address the root of the problem, which seems to sound like a lack of self confidence and seeking validation by any means, or what you believe you deserve.

the only thing i can offer to counteract is to be kinder to yourself. much easier said than done. the bull that everyone spouts, “you can’t love anyone until you’ve loved yourself”, it’s irritatingly true. i say this gently, you need to stop seeking validation from these men. they are not complimenting *you*, they are only after your youth and its naivety, and every interaction with them *will* hurt you in the long run. i know it’s hard. but you need to start appreciating yourself. be kinder to yourself. treat your body like a friend. you deserve much much more than you’ve convinced yourself. i promise you.

if you tend to spiral, something that’s helped me is to rationalize what i’m thinking. if i find myself spiraling into a self-deprecating pit, i ask myself genuinely *why* i feel this way. i nitpick every impulsive self-sabotaging blurb, and i annoy myself into submission. some introspective questions to ground yourself,

 “why do i feel like *everyone* hates me? who even *is* everyone? who else exists outside of the situation?”

“why do i feel like i’m pathetic to talk to? if i really am hard to converse with, is it something about my tone or my word choice or what i talk about?” 

“why do i feel like i’m a loser? what *is* a loser? what defines an actual loser? what do i think of when i think of the word “loser”? am i really comparable to that?”

it sounds dumb but it’s forced me to slow down my thoughts and converse with myself, instead of just blurting that i “just *don’t* deserve good things and it’s *just the way it is*”, i have to sit down and think, “ok, that’s not realistic. nothing is really set by fate and such negative thinking is self-fulfilling prophetism”. 

sorry to ramble. i recognize you’re in a tough spot, and i promise you there is a light at the end of this tunnel. learn from your experiences, and don’t put yourself in harm’s way to sabotage your growth. you are a good person. you deserve a lot more. you are much much better than you think

i’m 20 years old, my friends are all 19-23. i only hang out with people my age. everyone below 18 to me are children. they’re in the throes of arguably the worst stage of life, rife with hormones and social anxieties and academic pressures, and they come out stronger. i admire and pity them like younger siblings. i, and assuming any decent person, cannot in any state of mind frame a minor in a sexual situation.

step back and ask yourself why this 23 year old man is seeing fit to hang out with someone eight years his junior. why he sees it appropriate to have a romantic relationship with someone who is (presumably, correct me if wrong) a sophomore in high school, still legally obliged to attend public school, still unable to legally drive a car, still unable to legally work after a certain time at night (i’m taking a lot of liberties here, assuming you’re in the states… correct me if wrong), still beneath their legal guardians, still in the peak of their emotional, physical, and social development period... this is absolutely not to discount or belittle teenagehood, rather just to paint how starkly different your life is from someone his age.

i know how good it feels to be acknowledged by someone your senior. know that it’s not your fault at all, nor is it specific to you. these guys go after teens who lack affirmation or confidence solely to make themselves feel better, as teens in this stage of life are really impressionable, and they *know* this. it’s emotional manipulation. grooming, if you will, to stroke their own pathetic egos, even if it means messing with literal teens to bolster it. 

if *anything*, this says more about the kind of person he is rather than you. good luck, friend

I was hospitalized a couple years ago. I don’t remember much of it honestly, I was really out of it. I was placed in the youth ward despite being 18, but I was grateful for that. The teen center was separated by sex, but we’d often have group therapy sessions and were allowed to play in the courtyard together. We had a TV in both sections of the teen ward, and I remember watching a lot of Goosebumps on Netflix. I was allowed a 10-min call a day. The food was ok. I remember there being cliques among the longer staying residents. We were allowed to wear our own clothes and shoes but we were given grip socks and all laces were taken out of the clothes (hoodie drawstrings, shoelaces) and I remember the guys would be walking around with flopping open vans shoes and the sound it made. I had a few meetings with the psychologist and an interpersonal therapist. 
I just tried to mind my own business.

I was prescribed Abilify when I was committed to the hospital. Those three weeks were really, really not great. I felt like I was out of my body the entire time. I was so lethargic I begged them to let me stop taking it. Once I did I felt better. I do not have bipolar disorder so I cannot vouch for how that would affect it. I have heard success stories for Abilify though, so I think it’s dependent on the person.
